# `schema-widened`

The schema accepts more values

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `schema-widened` (both directions), `schema-widened-in-request`, `schema-widened-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Core variance rules (fallbacks) ([RULES.md section 1](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

Fallback for a schema change that no specific rule matches, where the new schema accepts more values than the old one.

## Why this default

In requests: old clients keep sending values that are still valid. In responses: clients may receive values they were not written to handle.

## Example

From test case [`schema-widened`](../../test/cases/schema-widened/): 'not' removed: the schema accepts more values.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           not:
-             const: ''
```

Findings:

- `schema-widened-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

3 test cases expect this rule. Each folder has the base and revision documents and the expected findings; they run with `npm test`.

| Test case | Expects | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| [`schema-widened`](../../test/cases/schema-widened/) | `schema-widened-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet | 'not' removed: the schema accepts more values. |
| [`type-narrowed-union`](../../test/cases/type-narrowed-union/) | `schema-widened-in-request` · info · #/components/schemas/Pet | A oneOf of an object and a string replaced by an inline object: the union's types are its branches' types, so string was dropped. |
| [`type-union-to-inline-object`](../../test/cases/type-union-to-inline-object/) | `schema-widened-in-request` · info · #/components/schemas/Pet | A oneOf of object schemas (one through allOf) replaced by an inline object: the type is object on both sides, so no type-narrowed. The union's removal is still reported. |

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  schema-widened: warn
```

## How to fix

In responses, only send the new values to clients that ask for them, or document that clients must tolerate them.
